newsitem.title: UK: Cocoa deficit may be smaller than forecast - broker.
newsitem.headline: Cocoa deficit may be smaller than forecast - broker.

text.p: The global cocoa production deficit in the 1996/97 marketing year (Oct/Sep) is likely to be much smaller than early forecasts which range from 100,000 to 200,000 tonnes, according to U.S. commodity brokers Merrill Lynch.
In its latest biweekly report Merrill Lynch projected a cocoa deficit of 87,000 tonnes compared to an estimated surplus of 60,000 tonnes in 1995/96.

"We think the production deficit will be substantially smaller and this is the main fundamental reason why the cocoa market has not been able to extend gains much above the $1,400 level (basis New York) recently," Merrill Lynch said.
The deficit forecast was based on a gross output projection of 2.69 million tonnes, down by 90,000 tonnes from 1995/96, and global consumption increasing by 53,000 tonnes to 2.75 million tonnes.

"The combined stock change between the two seasons would be a drop of only 27,000 tonnes, hardly enough to make a dent in the global stockpile and turn us wildly enthusiastic about this market," Merrill Lynch said.

But Ivorian and Ghanaian sales were easing since much of the new crop and some of the 1997/98 crop has already been hedged forward. These sales could accelerate however if the price of cocoa became attractive.
Futures prices in London are recovering from lows of around 975 stg a tonne basis the March contract but traders say sentiment remains bearish with heavy resistance above the market.
